name: 15d mixture of experts routing
title: A router sends each token to its two highest scoring experts
subtitle: Four experts, top-2 routing, six tokens; bars are router probabilities after softmax

steps.caption: Token 1 has router scores (2.0, 1.0, 0.5, -1.0). Softmax turns them into probabilities 0.61, 0.22, 0.14 and 0.03, and top-2 routing keeps experts 1 and 2.
Renormalizing the two kept probabilities gives weights 0.731 and 0.269. If expert 1 returns (1, 0) and expert 2 returns (0, 2), the layer outputs 0.731 x (1, 0) + 0.269 x (0, 2) = (0.731, 0.538).
Token 2 goes to experts 2 and 3. Only those two experts run for it. The other two hold their weights in memory and do no arithmetic for this token.
Token 3 goes to experts 1 and 2. Only those two experts run for it. The other two hold their weights in memory and do no arithmetic for this token.
Token 4 goes to experts 3 and 4. Only those two experts run for it. The other two hold their weights in memory and do no arithmetic for this token.
Token 5 goes to experts 1 and 2. Only those two experts run for it. The other two hold their weights in memory and do no arithmetic for this token.
Token 6 goes to experts 1 and 2. Only those two experts run for it. The other two hold their weights in memory and do no arithmetic for this token.
Six tokens make 12 assignments, a fair share of 3 per expert. Expert 2 received 5 and expert 4 only 1. Left uncorrected this imbalance grows, which is why training adds a load balancing loss.
Each expert holds 3 x 384 x 1,024 = 1.18M weights. Eight per block gives 60.58M stored, 121.2 MB in bf16, while each token multiplies against 18.11M.
steps.heading: In the story model total parameters grow with experts but active ones grow with k
